doc.title: Donn Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 6, 2009

title: Transportation troubles and the hearse idea
summary: Borrowing cars for gigs and his mother's refusal to fund a used hearse.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Yeah and I bought a couple of his CDs, and frankly, I like the way he played back then better than, of course he’s recognized as one of the premier bassists in the world. And there were a couple of other instances where we had to bring in somebody else, and it’s just been a lot of phone calls and making sure that they get picked up or whatever. And that was the trying part of it, it wasn’t a very simple thing. Transportation was a bug because I didn’t have a car and I had to borrow cars all the time and I once, I think I was talking to Phil and I said, “You know, why don’t we go buy a used hearse? It’s big, you could fit the whole band in there, you know, we’d paint it or put something in the windows.” So when I got home on vacation I asked my mother if she would loan me some money to buy a vehicle. And she said, “What?” And I said I’d like to buy a used hearse.” She said, “Absolutely not. I will not have a hearse parked anywhere near my house.”
I can’t say as a blame her.
